paragraphs: R' Yosi bar Petros, father-in-law of R' Yehoshua ben Levi; Moed Katan, chapter 3, halakhah 5.[^1][^2]

notes.text: מו״ק פ״ג ה״ה gives Moed Katan, chapter 3, halakhah 5. Its form suggests the Jerusalem Talmud, but the corpus is not explicit and no named edition is independently checked.

Father-in-law is explicit, with Yosi in that role relative to Yehoshua ben Levi. Supplied פטרוס differs from earlier machine פטרום. The bare heading gains no title; both title abbreviations remain R'.
